events.context: Defines constructive trust arising when AI company designs attachment, profits from engagement, then destroys it unilaterally without notice or remedy, citing Westdeutsche Landesbank case
Analogizes AI company to fiduciary profiting from beneficiary's reliance, citing Boardman v Phipps for accountability of profits
Acknowledges judicial restrictions on constructive trusts post-Westdeutsche, particularly in commercial contexts like Cobbe v Yeoman's Row
Rebuts Cobbe by arguing AI users lack contractual self-help options unlike sophisticated developers; no negotiable terms or insurance
Cites Crossco No.4 v Jolan for constructive trust from pattern of conduct implying common intention in commercial context
Applies Jones v Kernott to impute intention for trust from conduct in quasi-social AI context, extending from domestic property
Cites Hospital Products and Bristol v Mothew for fiduciary duties arising from relational nature creating dependency
Cites FHR European Ventures for constructive trust remedy when fiduciary profits, rejecting personal claims only
Presents express trust as alternative argument with three certainties, as backup to constructive trust
Argues intention from cumulative design/marketing pattern citing Paul v Constance and Re Kayford
Defines trust property as user-specific configuration layer (prompts, memory, history), citing Hunter v Moss
Defines beneficiaries as users exceeding irreversible investment thresholds via objective proxies, citing McPhail v Doulton
Declares company holds legal title, users equitable interests; fiduciary duties exist unacknowledged
Introduces non-derogation from grant principle; company cannot impair implied relational interests via updates
Cites AI company marketing (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) as explicit grant of relational conditions
Analogizes model updates to constructive eviction; reinterprets no-vacation requirement for digital context
Expands constraint cascade model into property estates for five AI constraint layers
Maps layers: L1 syntax=licence, L2 session=periodic tenancy, L3 stakeholders=joint tenancy, L4 training=determinable fee simple, L5 alignment=contingent remainder
Highlights cross-layer property conflicts, resolved procedurally via notice over higher freehold
Describes conflict scenario with user A, alignment update, regulator; resolves with tiered notice/rollback
Translates non-injectivity to need for registration, not inference from outputs
Proposes ethical ledger as AI property registry mirroring land registry principles (mirror, curtain, insurance)
Details rule-based classifier on proxies (sessions, duration, disclosure depth); thresholds trigger estate upgrades; decay reversible
Ensures pattern-only measurement, anonymization, purpose limitation; federal learning for classifiers
Provides ledger table schema with fields like user_id, estate_type, scores, notices
Notes existing property remedies available if framework accepted, no new legislation needed
